intent: Let clients optionally set an expiry in days when creating a short link, so that the redirect endpoint returns 410 Gone once the link has expired, while links created without an expiry never expire.

functional_needs.statement: POST /api/links accepts an optional expiry value, expressed in days, when a short link is created.
functional_needs.source_quote: when creating a short link the client may give an expiry in days

functional_needs.statement: Once a link's expiry has passed, GET /{code} returns 410 Gone instead of a 302 redirect.
functional_needs.source_quote: After it expires, the redirect returns 410 Gone instead of redirecting.

functional_needs.statement: A link created without an expiry never expires. This includes all links that existed before this change. Such links keep redirecting with 302 indefinitely.
functional_needs.source_quote: Links without an expiry never expire.

functional_needs.statement: The only valid expiry values are whole-number JSON integers from 1 to 3650 inclusive.
functional_needs.source_quote: Accept only whole-number JSON integers from 1 to 3650 inclusive.

functional_needs.statement: An expiry value that is zero, negative, fractional, a string (e.g. "7") or outside 1..3650 is rejected with 400 application/problem+json. The detail must describe the expiry problem.
functional_needs.source_quote: Reject zero, negative, fractional, string and out-of-range values with 400 application/problem+json whose detail describes the expiry problem.

functional_needs.statement: When an expiry value is rejected, no link is persisted.
A 410 response for an expired link does not change clickCount or lastClickedAt. Only successful 302 redirects are counted.
functional_needs.source_quote: Only successful 302 redirects are counted. A 410 response leaves clickCount and lastClickedAt unchanged.

functional_needs.statement: For an expired link, GET /api/links/{code} and GET /api/links/{code}/analytics keep returning 200 with their current fields. Only the redirect endpoint returns 410.
functional_needs.source_quote: Keep returning 200 with the current fields. Only the redirect endpoint returns 410.

functional_needs.statement: No new response field (such as expiresAt) is added. Create and details responses stay exactly as they are today.
functional_needs.source_quote: Do not add any new response field. Keep create and details responses exactly as today

functional_needs.statement: Compatibility: a create request without an expiry field still returns 201 with the same Location header and body as today.
functional_needs.source_quote: Keep create and details responses exactly as today

functional_needs.statement: Compatibility: for a link that has not expired, GET /{code} still returns 302 with Location set to the long URL and Cache-Control: no-store, and increments clickCount by exactly one and updates lastClickedAt.
Compatibility: GET /{code} for an unknown code still returns 404, not 410. 410 is returned only for existing links that have expired.
functional_needs.source_quote: After it expires, the redirect returns 410 Gone

functional_needs.statement: Compatibility: the 410 response uses the existing application/problem+json error format (type, title, status, detail) with title 'Gone'.
Compatibility: unknown JSON properties in the create request (e.g. "alias") are still ignored and the request still returns 201. Strict type checking applies only to the expiry field.
functional_needs.source_quote: the client may give an expiry in days

ambiguities.question: What exact name should the optional expiry field have in the POST /api/links JSON body?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: The field name is part of the public API contract. Clients and acceptance tests must send exactly this name. Because unknown properties are ignored, a misnamed field would be silently dropped and the link would never expire.

ambiguities.question: How should an explicit JSON null for the expiry field be treated?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: It decides whether {"url":...,"expiresInDays":null} returns 201 with a never-expiring link or 400.
ambiguities.recommended_default: Treat explicit null the same as an absent field: return 201 and create a link that never expires.

ambiguities.question: Is a JSON number with an integral value but written with a fraction or exponent (e.g. 7.0 or 7e0) a valid 'whole-number JSON integer'?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: It decides whether such inputs return 201 or 400 under C-1.
ambiguities.recommended_default: Reject with 400. Only JSON integer literals are accepted.
options: Accept if the value is integral

ambiguities.question: How is the expiry instant defined, and is a link expired at exactly that instant?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: It sets the exact moment a link switches from 302 to 410. The difference is only observable at the boundary.
ambiguities.recommended_default: expiresAt = createdAt + N × 24 hours (UTC). The link is expired when now >= expiresAt.
options: createdAt + N×24h, expired when now >= expiresAt
createdAt + N×24h, expired when now > expiresAt
End of the Nth calendar day (UTC) after creation

ambiguities.question: What detail text and headers should the 410 problem+json response carry?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: Clients may display or log the detail. Caching headers affect whether intermediaries cache the 410.
ambiguities.recommended_default: Return status 410, title 'Gone', and a detail such as 'short link has expired', with Cache-Control: no-store as on the redirect.
options: Generic detail with no cache header

out_of_scope: Adding any new response field (e.g. expiresAt) to the create or details responses (per C-4)
Returning 410 from GET /api/links/{code} or GET /api/links/{code}/analytics for expired links (per C-3)
Counting clicks or updating lastClickedAt on 410 responses (per C-2)
Expiry units other than whole days, and values outside 1..3650 (per C-1)
Changing or removing a link's expiry after creation (not requested)
Deleting or purging expired links (not requested)
